title: Vendor-neutral telemetry adapter contract + conformance suite (two commits, never squashed)
wave: Wave 4 (with W11; W11 lands first — W10 follows because its two commits must not be squashed and its commit 2 carries the highest per-LOC regression risk in the milestone)
one_line: Add a small vendor-neutral span interface (with a NOOP, an in-memory reference implementation, and a shared conformance suite) that every future telemetry backend can implement, then wire the existing OpenTelemetry path underneath it as the default adapter without changing a single exported signature or a single line of the existing OTEL test.
user_visible_effect: none in milestone 1 — this is internal. No setting, no output, no flag, no dependency change. The payoff is that a later milestone can ship a Sentry or structured-log telemetry backend without forking telemetry.ts, and without forcing a non-OTEL backend to depend on @opentelemetry/api.

steps.instruction: Create the contract. Name the span interface `TelemetrySpan`, NOT `Span` — packages/agent/src/index.ts:24 already star-exports telemetry.ts, which re-exports OTEL's `Span` at telemetry.ts:2106, so a second star-exported `Span` makes `bun run check:ts` fail with TS2308. Include `end(): void` on the interface (7 span.end() call sites exist today and the span handle outlives the call). Widen TelemetryAttributeValue to include readonly string[] and readonly number[] (telemetry.ts:755 and :764 assign string arrays). Give setStatus a second optional `message` parameter (all 5 setStatus sites pass one). Zero imports from outside this directory.

Create the NOOP context. `startSpan` must be `return fn(NOOP_SPAN)` — no try/catch, no wrapper, no transformation. The return value must be the callback's own return value, by identity, for every T including promises, undefined, and objects.

Create the in-memory reference adapter. Expose a `createMemoryTelemetryContext()` factory returning both the TelemetryContext and a readable record list (name, parent, events, attributes, status, statusMessage, ended). Parent linkage must come from an explicit enclosing-span stack, not from ambient context, so parentage is deterministic and testable.

Create the suite as `createCase(factory, group, name, test)` entries plus a `runConformance(factory)` driver. Write one case per distinct branch: parentage, event recording, status transition (ok and error, and unset-by-default), attribute round-trip, array-valued attribute round-trip, end() idempotence, callback return passthrough. Do not import noop.ts or memory.ts here.
Add the star barrel with extensionless specifiers.

Add `export * from "./telemetry/context";` immediately after line 24. Then run `bun run check:types` in packages/agent and confirm it is green — this is the step that catches TS2308 if step 1 was done wrong.

Run the suite against BOTH the memory adapter and NOOP. Add the dedicated NOOP negative assertion: `expect(NOOP_TELEMETRY_CONTEXT.startSpan(ctx, 'n', () => sentinel)).toBe(sentinel)` — `toBe` (identity), not `toEqual`. Run `bun test packages/agent/test/telemetry-conformance.test.ts`.

`bun run check:ts` green, conformance test green, and `git diff --stat` must show ONLY the six new files plus the one-line index.ts change. Commit 1 must not touch telemetry.ts or any production path. Land and merge before starting commit 2.

Add an OTEL-backed implementation of the contract. Route the private `startSpan` through it, keeping its existing signature and its existing attribute-assembly order byte-for-byte (attribute precedence at :466-491 is load-bearing: operation → model → conversation → agent → config → dynamic → caller). Do not reorder.

Route `runInActiveSpan` through the contract's activation hook, preserving the OTEL-context semantics its doc comment describes (startSpan creates but does not activate; the wrapper is what makes downstream provider/MCP spans attach as children). Keep it exported with the same signature — it is part of the public surface.

Confirm OTEL is still the default path and nothing else moved: `git diff --stat packages/agent/test/otel.test.ts` MUST be empty. If it is not empty, STOP — do not edit the test to make it pass. Then run `bun test packages/agent/test/otel.test.ts` once the native addon is built.

Add one line under `## [Unreleased]` in packages/agent/CHANGELOG.md (it is an internal refactor, so `### Changed` and worded as the user-visible absence of change, or omit — a human decides). Then verify `git log` shows W10 as exactly two separate commits, never squashed.

test_contract: The observable contract is: an implementation of TelemetryContext can be swapped in and every telemetry behaviour omp exposes stays identical. Concretely the tests defend four things. (1) SPAN PARENTAGE — a span started inside another span's callback records the enclosing span as its parent, never root; a consumer debugging a run in a non-OTEL backend sees the same tree shape they see in OTEL today. (2) EVENT + STATUS — addEvent and setStatus on the vendor-neutral surface produce the same span events and the same status.code a downstream OTEL exporter would see; otel.test.ts:246,317,337,384 are the existing proof for the OTEL side. (3) NOOP IDENTITY — NOOP_TELEMETRY_CONTEXT.startSpan returns the callback's return value by identity and records nothing; if this regresses, every code path that does `return telemetry.startSpan(..., () => computeSomething())` silently returns undefined, which is a wrong-answer bug that no assertion on OTEL output would catch. (4) ARRAY ATTRIBUTES AND STATUS MESSAGES — string[] attributes and setStatus messages survive the round trip; these are the two sites otel.test.ts does NOT cover, so if the contract is too narrow the ONLY thing that catches it is this suite. Consumer-visible failure if the contract regresses: a future Sentry or structured-log backend either fails to typecheck against the contract, or ships and silently drops stop sequences, available-tool lists, and every error message on failed spans.

COMMIT 1: (a) `cd packages/agent && bun run check:types` is green — this is the load-bearing gate and it is the ONLY one that is currently runnable; (b) `git diff --stat` lists exactly six new files under packages/agent/src/telemetry/ plus a one-line change to packages/agent/src/index.ts, and nothing else — in particular telemetry.ts must show zero lines changed; (c) `git log` shows commit 1 as its own commit.

gate_can_fail: Yes for the type gate, and it was demonstrated failing rather than assumed. I reproduced the exact failure mode in an isolated scratch project: with `export * from "./telem"` and `export * from "./telem/context"` where both export an interface named `Span`, tsc emits `error TS2308: Module "./telem" has already exported a member named 'Span'`. Since telemetry.ts:2106 re-exports OTEL's `Span` and the plan mandates adding a second star-export to packages/agent/src/index.ts, following the plan's §F8 interface name verbatim WILL turn `bun run check:types` red. Renaming to `TelemetrySpan` is what makes it green — so the gate discriminates between the right and wrong implementation. The commit-2 gate (`git diff --stat` on otel.test.ts) is also genuinely falsifiable: it goes non-empty the instant anyone edits that file, which is precisely the failure the plan is trying to prevent. The only caveat: the behavioural half of both gates is currently unrunnable because the native addon is not built, so on Monday the type gate is real and the test gate is a promise.
effort: M, but asymmetric: commit 1 is S (four small dependency-free files, one barrel line, one test) and commit 2 is the M half. Under the C17 reading this spec adopts, commit 2 is a ~40 LOC seam at two private/public functions rather than a rewrite of 2114 LOC, which is what brings the total to M instead of L.
risk: The highest per-LOC regression risk in the milestone. telemetry.ts sits on every agent path, so a regression here is a production incident and not a red test. The specific trap: designing the contract from the plan's §F8 sketch, which cannot express omp's actual span lifecycle (no `end()`, and a callback-scoped span when the handle escapes across an await) and is too narrow on attribute types — and then discovering the only thing that catches the resulting silent attribute loss is a suite you are writing at the same time as the thing it is supposed to police. Second trap: the temptation to make otel.test.ts pass by editing it. Do not. Third trap: the plan's own C17 correction contradicts its §W10/§F8 instruction, so an engineer who reads only §F8 will build the wrong commit 2.
open_questions: Should TelemetryAttributes accept `null | undefined` values, as OTEL's own AttributeValue does? I checked node_modules: OTEL's AttributeValue is `string | number | boolean | Array<null|undefined|string> | Array<null|undefined|number> | Array<null|undefined|boolean>` and Attributes allows `AttributeValue | undefined`. I specified the narrower readonly string[]/number[] because it is what omp actually assigns today, but a future backend may want null. A human should pick: match OTEL exactly, or stay narrow and widen when a backend needs it.

Is `conformance.ts` shipped in the published `src` tree or dev-only? packages/agent/package.json has `files: ["src"]` and main/types point at source, so a conformance module in src ships to every consumer. It is harmless (pure, dependency-free) but it is a deliberate choice, not an accident — confirm it is intended rather than a test-only module that belongs in test/.

Should the contract be exported from the package root at all in milestone 1, or held internal with a named owner? The plan calls the barrel line mandatory; I agree, because commit 2's premise depends on it. But it does mean a public API commitment is being made in a milestone that is explicitly not user-facing. Worth an explicit yes/no from the maintainer before merging commit 1.

Is the second W10 (CI/release/Docker/homebrew/nix rename, plan line 7962) or the third W10 (collab transport watchdog, plan line 8544) the one on someone's board this week? The ID is reused three times in one document. The spec here is unambiguously the telemetry one (Wave 4, lines 1347-1429) but a ticket board keyed on 'W10' will collide.

plan_corrections.claim: §F8 / §W10: the contract is `interface Span { addEvent; setAttributes; setStatus }` plus a callback-based `startSpan<T>(context, name, fn)`.
plan_corrections.verdict: wrong — the contract as written cannot express omp's span lifecycle at all
plan_corrections.correction: There is no `end()` on the interface and the span is scoped to the callback, but omp's spans are NOT callback-scoped: startChatSpan (telemetry.ts:693) RETURNS a handle, which is handed to finishChatSpan (telemetry.ts:1116) across an await boundary, which calls span.end() at :1162. There are 7 `span.end()` call sites total, none of them inside the creating callback. A span that cannot be ended cannot be implemented. I added `end(): void` to the interface. Keep the callback form too — it is what models runInActiveSpan (:2048) — but the interface must carry end().
plan_corrections.evidence: `grep -c '\.end()' packages/agent/src/telemetry.ts` -> 7, at lines 1162, 1195, 1634, 1880, 1951, 2093 (plus one doc mention at 383). startChatSpan signature at :693-701 returns `Span | undefined`; finishChatSpan at :1116-1118 takes `span: Span | undefined` as a separate async call.

Star-exporting a second interface named `Span` from the same barrel makes `bun run check:ts` fail. Name the contract's interface `TelemetrySpan` and export the bare OTEL `Span` untouched. I verified this by compiling the exact shape, not by reasoning about it.

plan_corrections.claim: §W10 and §F8: otel.test.ts (1152 LOC) is the safety net for commit 2, and it passing with a zero-line diff is the proof of behavior preservation.
plan_corrections.verdict: partly-wrong — it is a real net but has two blind spots, and both sit exactly where the contract is most likely to be wrong
plan_corrections.correction: otel.test.ts has ZERO assertions on RequestStopSequences or RequestAvailableTools, and zero anywhere in packages/agent/test for stopSequences / availableTools / available_tools. It also asserts only on `status.code` (lines 246, 317, 337, 384) and never on `status.message`, while all 5 setStatus sites in telemetry.ts pass a message. So an adapter built on the plan's contract would silently drop stop sequences, available-tool lists, and every error message on failed spans, and the plan's own gate would stay green. The conformance suite MUST cover array-valued attributes and status messages, and the PR should say out loud that otel.test.ts does not cover them.
plan_corrections.evidence: `grep -n 'RequestStopSequences\|RequestAvailableTools' packages/agent/test/otel.test.ts` -> no matches. `git grep 'stopSequences|available_tools|availableTools' -- packages/agent/test` -> no matches. `grep -n 'status\.message' packages/agent/test/otel.test.ts` -> no matches; the four status assertions are all `.status.code`. setStatus sites: telemetry.ts:1187, 1190, 1547, 1872, 1949, all passing a message.
